2026-11-07.headline: SharePoint site skills guide now details creation, permissions, and lifecycle controls
2026-11-07.overview: The period brought one documentation update for Copilot in SharePoint. The revised guidance explains how site owners manage site skills from Settings > Site skills, including their storage, ownership, permissions, and lifecycle operations.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Site owners can use the documented management page and controls to administer site skills. No action is required.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management guidance expanded
keyChanges.detail: The Copilot in SharePoint article now documents creating and managing site skills from Settings > Site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions.

2026-11-09.headline: Sensitivity-labeled PDFs gain web annotation in OneDrive and SharePoint in January 2027
2026-11-09.overview: OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web are scheduled to let users with editing rights annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs without removing their labels. Saved files will retain both annotations and protections, with worldwide rollout planned for late January 2027.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: No admin action is required. Administrators should note that the capability applies only to OneDrive for Business and SharePoint and is intended for users with editing rights.

keyChanges.title: Editing rights will include annotation of protected PDFs
keyChanges.detail: Users with editing rights will be able to annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs on the web without removing the labels. Annotations and protections will be preserved when the file is saved; worldwide rollout is planned for late January 2027.

2026-11-10.headline: Global navigation setup guidance now covers favorites, Teams, and rollout delays
2026-11-10.overview: The SharePoint app bar and global navigation guidance now describes personalized Favorites and Recents, plus quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive. It also clarifies requirements, permissions, Teams integration, and the possibility of a 24-hour rollout delay.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Administrators configuring the app bar or global navigation should review the updated requirements, Teams integration guidance, and user access expectations before deployment.

keyChanges.title: Updated global navigation setup guidance
keyChanges.detail: The page now documents personalized Favorites and Recents; quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive; global navigation requirements and permissions; Teams integration; and a possible 24-hour rollout delay.

2026-11-02.headline: Unified Copilot Search and group-permission governance reporting headline SharePoint administration
2026-11-02.overview: Two Message Center announcements carry the period: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are moving to a unified Copilot Search experience, with preview rollout beginning in mid-October 2026 and general rollout in mid-January 2027; SharePoint’s Data access governance report for group permissions is scheduled to roll out worldwide from late November to early December. A separate Agents and Copilot article now documents the full site-skills management workflow.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Copilot Search requires minimal organizational action, and users can opt out during preview. Administrators can use the forthcoming report in the admin center to find sites accessible to particular groups and assess access levels, supporting permission reviews and checks for unintended content exposure. Site owners can administer skills from Settings > Site skills using the documented controls; the article states that no action is required.

keyChanges.title: Copilot Search unifies SharePoint Online and OneDrive web search
keyChanges.detail: The updated experience adds natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters. The announced schedule places preview rollout from mid-October 2026 and general rollout from mid-January 2027; users can opt out during preview and organizational action is minimal.
keyChanges.product: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web

keyChanges.title: Data access governance report adds group-permission visibility
keyChanges.detail: The new report in the SharePoint admin center will help administrators identify sites accessible to specific groups and assess their access levels. Worldwide rollout is scheduled from late November to early December 2026, supporting permission management and efforts to prevent unintended content exposure.

keyChanges.title: Site skills management is documented under Settings > Site skills
keyChanges.detail: The updated article explains how to create and manage site skills, including uploading, editing, enabling, disabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting them. It also clarifies storage, ownership, and permissions, giving site owners a documented management path.

2026-11-09.headline: SharePoint plans protected PDF annotation and pay-as-you-go storage overages
2026-11-09.overview: Microsoft announced two planned SharePoint changes: web annotation for sensitivity-label-protected PDFs and an opt-in pay-as-you-go meter for storage beyond the included quota. A separate global-navigation article now provides more precise app-bar guidance on features, permissions, Teams integration, and rollout timing.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: No admin action is required for protected PDF annotation. Administrators considering the storage meter should account for its opt-in model, Azure billing-permission requirement, and integration with Microsoft 365 Archive. Review the global-navigation guidance when configuring the app bar, particularly for permissions, Teams integration, and the possible 24-hour rollout delay.

keyChanges.title: Protected PDFs will support browser annotation
keyChanges.detail: OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web will let users with editing rights annotate sensitivity-label-protected PDFs without removing the labels. Annotations and protections remain when the file is saved. Worldwide rollout is planned for late January 2027, with no admin action required.

keyChanges.title: Extra SharePoint storage will gain pay-as-you-go billing
keyChanges.detail: An opt-in consumption-based meter will charge for SharePoint storage used beyond the included quota. The model is planned for global rollout in January 2027, integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive, and requires Azure billing permissions.

keyChanges.title: Global-navigation guidance now covers app-bar access and rollout details
keyChanges.detail: The updated setup guidance describes personalized favorites and recents, plus quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive. It also spells out global-navigation requirements, permissions, Teams integration, and a possible 24-hour rollout delay.

2026-11.headline: Unified Copilot Search and group-permission reporting set SharePoint’s next priorities
2026-11.overview: November’s most consequential changes are planned rollouts: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are moving to unified Copilot Search with natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters, while a new admin-center report will expose sites accessible to specific groups. Microsoft also announced opt-in billing for SharePoint storage overages and web annotation for sensitivity-label-protected PDFs. Documentation updates added operational detail: global-navigation guidance now covers permissions, Teams integration, and a possible 24-hour delay, while the site-skills article documents management from Settings > Site skills, including enabling, copying, restoring, downloading, and deleting skills.
2026-11.adminImpact: Track the Copilot Search preview and general-rollout timeline; users can opt out during preview and Microsoft says organizational action is minimal. Use the Data access governance report for group-permission reviews when it arrives. The storage meter is opt-in and requires Azure billing permissions, while protected-PDF annotation requires no administrator action. Administrators configuring global navigation should review permissions and Teams integration and allow for the possible 24-hour rollout delay; site owners can manage skills from Settings > Site skills.

keyChanges.title: Unified Copilot Search brings AI-driven web search to SharePoint and OneDrive
keyChanges.detail: SharePoint Online and OneDrive for the web are updating to a unified Copilot Search experience with natural-language prompts, AI summaries, and filters. Preview rollout began in mid-October 2026, general rollout is planned for mid-January 2027, and users can opt out during preview.

keyChanges.title: Data access governance report targets group-permission exposure
keyChanges.detail: A new report in the SharePoint admin center will help administrators identify sites accessible to specific groups and assess their access levels. Worldwide rollout is planned from late November through early December 2026, supporting permission management and checks for unintended content exposure.

keyChanges.title: Opt-in meter introduces pay-as-you-go billing for SharePoint storage overages
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is introducing a consumption-based model for storage beyond the included SharePoint quota, allowing organizations to pay for extra storage used. The feature rolls out globally in January 2027, integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive, and requires Azure billing permissions.

keyChanges.title: Web annotation preserves labels on sensitivity-protected PDFs
keyChanges.detail: Users with editing rights will be able to annotate sensitivity-label-protected PDFs in OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web without removing the labels. Annotations and protections remain intact when files are saved; worldwide rollout is planned for late January 2027 and requires no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Global-navigation guidance clarifies app-bar configuration and rollout timing
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance now describes personalized favorites and recents, quick access to Discover, Publish, Build, and OneDrive, plus global-navigation requirements, permissions, Teams integration, and a possible 24-hour rollout delay. It gives administrators more precise configuration and user-access expectations.
